<handout>
# Lab 4: Debounced button toggle (mock handout)

> Mock handout written for testing `grader make-plan`. It is not an official course
> document.

## Goal

Use a push button to toggle an LED, and report each change over a serial port.

## Hardware

* A push button between pin **D2** and GND. There is no external resistor, so use the
  internal pull-up (`INPUT_PULLUP`). The button reads LOW while pressed.
* The on-board LED on pin **D13**.
* **Serial1** (pins D0/D1), not the USB `Serial` port, at **9600 baud**.

## Requirements

1. The LED is **off** after reset.
2. Each press of the button toggles the LED: the first press turns it on, the next one
   turns it off, and so on.
3. The LED must react **quickly**: a user should not notice any delay.
4. Real buttons bounce. One press must toggle the LED exactly **once**, no matter how
   much the contacts bounce.
5. On every toggle, print `ON` or `OFF` (the new state) on its own line on Serial1.
6. Implement debouncing in software, without blocking `delay()` calls.
7. Comment your code.

## Submission

Submit your sketch folder.
</handout>

<pin_map>
# Student board (Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense) pin name -> measuring board (Nucleo-L476RG) pin.
# Capabilities are from the MEASURING board's point of view (uart_rx = STM32 receives).
#
# !!! Every stm32 value is a PLACEHOLDER until verified in STM32CubeMX against the wiring. !!!
pins:
  D5:  { stm32: PA0,  caps: [gpio, timer_capture] }   # placeholder, verify in CubeMX (TIM2_CH1?)
  D2:  { stm32: TBD,  caps: [gpio, drive] }           # placeholder, button input on the student side
  D13: { stm32: TBD,  caps: [gpio, timer_capture] }   # placeholder, on-board LED on the Nano
  D1:  { stm32: PA10, caps: [uart_rx] }               # Nano Serial1 TX -> STM32 USART1 RX (placeholder)
  D0:  { stm32: PA9,  caps: [uart_tx] }               # Nano Serial1 RX <- STM32 USART1 TX (placeholder)
  A0:  { stm32: TBD,  caps: [analog_in, dac] }        # placeholder; L476 DAC1_OUT1 is PA4
  A4:  { stm32: TBD,  caps: [i2c_sda] }               # placeholder, STM32 acts as I2C target
  A5:  { stm32: TBD,  caps: [i2c_scl] }               # placeholder
  # Rig only, never used by a plan: open-drain line from the STM32 to the Nano's RST pin.
  RST: { stm32: PA1,  caps: [reset] }                 # Nucleo A1 -> Nano RST (open-drain, pulled low to reset)
</pin_map>

<primitives>
Each measurement primitive and the result fields it returns:
- freq_duty: frequency_hz, duty_pct, edge_count
- edge_delay: delay_ms, to_edge_count
- logic_trace: edge_count, final_level, edges_ms
- uart_read: text, byte_count, framing_errors
- i2c_log: read_count, write_count, transactions
- analog_read: mean_mv, min_mv, max_mv
</primitives>

plan.description: Verify debounced button-to-LED toggle on D2/D13 with ON/OFF reporting on Serial1, including fast reaction and single-toggle-per-bouncy-press behavior.

steps.requirement: The LED is off immediately after reset.
A clean button press turns the LED on (exactly one toggle edge).
The LED reacts quickly to a button press (within 50 ms, no noticeable delay).
On turning the LED on, the board prints 'ON' on its own line on Serial1.
A second, bouncy button press turns the LED off with exactly one toggle edge, proving debouncing works.
On turning the LED off, the board prints 'OFF' on its own line on Serial1.

assumptions: "Reacts quickly / no noticeable delay" is graded as an LED response within 50 ms of the button edge, since the handout gives no numeric bound.
A real bouncy press is simulated with 10 contact bounces at 2 ms intervals before settling low; this is treated as a representative bounce pattern since the handout gives no bounce profile.
UART text requirements are checked with a 'contains' match on "ON"/"OFF" rather than an exact full-line regex, to tolerate surrounding whitespace/newline formatting.
The button idle (unpressed) state is simulated by releasing the drive line, relying on the student's INPUT_PULLUP to read it high, matching the handout's wiring (no external resistor).

not_graded.requirement: Debouncing must be implemented in software without blocking delay() calls.
not_graded.reason: Implementation technique (blocking vs non-blocking code, use of millis() timers) cannot be determined from electrical behavior alone.
Source-code style/comments are not observable through electrical measurement.
